text:
erin: FYI repro in the node sampleapp: rapid reconnects (~80-180ms) after auth refresh cause the SSE parser to emit fragments out of order -> duplicate final token.

kai: repro pls?

erin: tiny script I used to stress it: 

``
// repro-loop.js
const es = new EventSource(url);
setTimeout(() => { es.close(); setTimeout(() => new EventSource(url), 120); }, 100);
// repeat in a loop
``

rachel: Trimmed logs: partial chunk A arrives, auth refresh -> new conn, chunk B parsed first, then leftover of A arrives. Parser treats them as separate chunks -> garbled JSON / duplicate final marker.

kai: Quick mitigation idea: add an opaque per-chunk sequence header from the server and have the client drop any chunk with seq <= lastSeen when a reconnect happens. Feature-flag it.

erin: I'll open a small PR `dropStaleChunksOnReconnect` (default off) and add an e2e in sampleapp CI that randomizes reconnect delays to catch flakiness. I'll file an issue too.

ci-bot: Created RED-3302: "sampleapp: fast reconnect causes fragment reordering" and added job devex/reconnect-frag-flaky.

infra-bot: Note: TCP CLOSE_WAIT/TIME_WAIT can amplify this; adding a short note to the infra runbook.

rachel: Long term we should rework parser to support fragment assembly across reconnects when Last-Event-Id is present, or ensure auth refresh emits a delimiter before swapping.

kai: Assigning reviewers @rachel and @erin.

erin: Thanks — will ping when PR lands :thumbsup:
